ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows two similar quadrilateral-like figures. The smaller blue figure on the left has area A = 525 cm^2, and its lower corresponding side is labeled x. The larger green figure on the right has area A = 1575 cm^2, and the corresponding lower side is labeled 18 cm. Reasoning: For similar figures, the ratio of areas equals the square of the ratio of corresponding side lengths. The large-to-small area ratio is 1575/525 = 3. Therefore the large-to-small linear scale factor is sqrt(3). Since the corresponding side lengths are 18 and x, 18/x = sqrt(3). Solving gives x = 18/sqrt(3) = 6sqrt(3) ≈ 10.392, which rounds to 10.4.
